procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory (prerequisite: factory located outside a free zone, MoIAT industrial licence, and MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added; takes about 3 working days).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The exporter ships the goods directly from the UAE to India; if transit through another country is necessary, it must be under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, or storage.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the e-service to apply for the Certificate of Origin for India; the exporter logs in, chooses the service, and fills in the application form.
The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product; each item on the certificate must qualify separately.
The exporter uploads the required documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 (band: invoice value up to AED 100000).
The exporter submits the application and receives approval, or a return with comments to correct; the Ministry of Foreign Trade processes the application in about one working day.

The competent authority issues the certificate prior to, at, or within five working days of export; retrospective issuance is possible up to 12 months from shipment with 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9.
The certificate is valid for twelve months from the date of issue and covers only one import (it may list several products).
The exporter prints the approved certificate.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020 including which origin criterion is claimed, keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing, and must answer a customs request within ten working days.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-works adjustment.
De minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).

Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022 via LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
Indirect materials (such as fuel, tools and consumables used in production) count as neither originating nor non-originating.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating; the last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.
